vo.text: Every month, millions of people in India pay back a loan. And every month, their lender sends them the same reminder, at the same time, as everyone else.
In one simulated campaign, that fixed schedule sent 1,262 messages. Only 23 replies came back.
Every one of those messages cost money. Almost all of them went unanswered.
Kairos works differently. Every morning, it looks at each borrower on their own: how late they are, how they replied before, and when they usually read their messages.
Then it makes one choice for each person: reach out today, or wait. If it reaches out, it picks the channel, SMS, WhatsApp, email or a voice call, and the hour that person is most likely to answer.
Before any message goes out, it has to get past Aladdin, our safety supervisor.

Aladdin asks the lender's questions. Has this person agreed to be contacted on this channel? Have they asked us to stop? Is it between 8 in the morning and 7 in the evening? Have we already contacted them enough this week? Is there budget left? Is their account on hold?
It asks when the message is planned, and again right before it is sent, in case anything has changed. If any answer is no, the message does not go.
This is Vikram. His EMI of ₹7,409 is 10 days late. Kairos sends him one SMS at 9:30 in the morning. Aladdin clears it. Vikram doesn't reply.
So the next day, Kairos waits instead of sending another reminder. On day 3, it tries WhatsApp. This time, Vikram replies: he will pay by the 29th.
Kairos recognises a promise to pay, and goes quiet. No more reminders. On day 7, the bank confirms ₹7,409. Reaching Vikram cost 65 paise.
Kairos learns from every reply. When we quietly made WhatsApp worse for one group, nobody told it. Within a week, it had moved them to SMS on its own.
Borrowers also write in on WhatsApp, at any hour. Kairos replies in seconds.
When is my EMI due?
To protect your account, I have sent a 6-digit code to your registered WhatsApp number.
Thank you, you are verified.
First, it made sure it was really her.
I already paid, here is the screenshot.
For your security, I can't help with this request in chat. A specialist from our team will review it.
That screenshot had been edited. Kairos checks every payment proof against the bank's records, so a fake one can never mark a loan as paid. It goes to a person instead.
When another borrower says she has lost her job, Kairos pauses her reminders and hands her to a person.
Stop.
You will not receive further automated reminders from us on any channel.
And when someone says stop, everything stops. SMS, WhatsApp, email and calls, all at once.
The team stays in charge, and Aladdin checks their actions too. Even a supervisor can't send a message at 8 at night.
In our simulated tests, Kairos recovered more for every rupee spent than a fixed schedule, without breaking a single rule.
